v1.1.0 — Planning-first rewrite for OpenClaw

**New**
- task_sync tool: 3-step retroactive record-keeping (survey → drill in → create done tasks)
- Cross-session & cross-agent continuity section: how any agent resumes work from any machine
- Quick Reference table covering all 13 tools

**Changed**
- Reframed from monitoring tool to planning-first tool: create hierarchy → review with user → execute
- Notes repositioned as audit trail attached to tasks, not agent memory
- Statuses reframed as shared checkpoints (open/wip/done/skipped) with explicit skipped discipline
- CONTEXT note on new task list is now a required step after create_task
- PROGRESS notes clarified: phase-level tasks only, not leaf tasks
- Subtask breakdown promoted as primary complexity management strategy, not exception handling

**Removed**
- generate_tasks tool (removed from Taskr API)
- Stale "coding-oriented rules" caveat
- Pre-described response schema paths (fragile and redundant — agents read live responses)

**Fixed**
- Project ID format updated to PR_00000000... pattern
- get_task_hierarchy response structure corrected

- Documentation streamlined and clarified for easier onboarding and setup.
- Setup instructions condensed, with clearer steps for obtaining and configuring credentials.
- Removed repetitive language and redundant sections to improve readability.
- Emphasized key workflow patterns and correct task/notes usage.
- Updated guidance around which task types and tools to use for non-coding/general agent work.

Summary: This update clarifies and strengthens guidance around when and how to use Taskr for transparent, persistent task tracking.

- Updated the description to better emphasize real-time transparency and cross-device monitoring benefits.
- Added explicit guidance to proactively offer Taskr for all substantial or multi-step work, not just when the user asks.
- Clarified which types of tasks are appropriate for Taskr and which are not.
- Added strict instruction to continue using Taskr for entire tracked workflows to prevent incomplete tasks in the dashboard.
- Introduced a Quick Reference section outlining the standard workflow loop and automatic status handling.
- Improved examples and phrasing to make workflow expectations and user communication clearer.

Initial public release of Taskr skill — remote task memory and tracking for OpenClaw.

- Enables agents to create, manage, and update persistent multi-step tasks, with real-time progress syncing to Taskr’s web and mobile dashboard.
- Includes setup instructions for environment variables and user onboarding via https://taskr.one.
- Emphasizes manual, structured task decomposition using `create_task` (not `generate_tasks`) for best general-purpose results.
- Documents key usage principles, such as “one task at a time” and durable context via notes.
- Supports transparent, observable workflows for any complex, multi-session work.
- Added guidance on authentication, API endpoints, and tool response structure.
